h: A scapegoat, a sorceress and a soap king's village
p: Pre-Raphaelite fans should head for The Scapegoat by William Holman Hunt, an eerie, unforgettable painting of a goat in a desolate landscape by the Dead Sea. Nearby you will find The Beguiling of Merlin by Edward Burne-Jones, a swirling, dreamlike scene of the wizard falling under a sorceress's spell. Both are among the gallery's best-known works.
Lever was also a big collector of items connected with Napoleon, so look out for that unexpected corner of the collection too.

Port Sunlight village was founded in 1888 to house workers at Lever's Sunlight Soap factory, and it is a fascinating example of a planned community, with each row of cottages designed in a different style. The Port Sunlight Museum on King George's Drive tells the story of the village and the people who lived there, and it makes a great companion to the gallery.
Allow two to three hours to see the gallery and stroll around the village. Christ Church, the village church, and the war memorial are both striking landmarks worth seeking out.

Getting there is easy, as Port Sunlight and Bebington stations are both on the Merseyrail network. If you have more time, the wider Wirral has lots to offer, from Ness Botanic Gardens and Wirral Country Park to the beach at West Kirby, or a classic Mersey Ferry ride across to Liverpool.
